choices.text: Leave the measure to the workers

outcomes.text: You hand back the cords. The workers lay them out for another comparison.

events.title: The frame before the performance
events.text: The performance cloth sags on its frame. A craft worker has brought spare wood, while the performer worries about the gathering that is approaching. They can use help with the joints, the fittings or the rehearsal.

choices.text: Fit the frame's wooden joints

outcomes.text: You measure the loose joints and fit replacements. The worker checks each cut before the cloth is hung again.

choices.text: Rehearse an entrance with the performer

outcomes.text: You repeat the entrance, waiting for the cue rather than rushing it. This time the next performer is ready when you finish.

choices.text: Read and count the required fittings

outcomes.text: You read the supply list and count the fittings aloud. Nothing is hidden beneath the spare wood when the final count is made.

choices.text: Leave them to prepare

outcomes.text: You step away from the frame. The craft worker reaches for the next fitting while the performer starts again.

events.title: Too many helpers at the door
events.text: Light supplies need moving between two rooms. The helpers keep meeting in the doorway, each sure their load should go first. The adult supervising them asks for a better arrangement.

choices.text: Divide the tasks and agree simple signals

outcomes.text: You count the loads, divide the tasks and agree on signals. When two helpers meet at the door again, you change the order.

choices.text: Hear the reasons for each proposed order

outcomes.text: You hear why each helper wants to go first. Once the tasks are divided, you explain which point they still disagree about.

choices.text: Check the supply list as each load arrives

outcomes.text: You check the bundles as they arrive. The supervisor confirms that one mark was made twice, and you correct the count.

choices.text: Let the supervisor arrange it

outcomes.text: You leave the doorway clear. The supervisor calls the helpers together to try again.

events.title: A line missing from the list
events.text: A calculator lays two copies of a day list beside one another. Their headings agree, but farther down the entries drift apart. There is room beside the table if you want to help find the mistake.

choices.text: Check the intervals between entries

outcomes.text: You count the intervals and find a line one copy has skipped. The calculator follows your marks and confirms the correction.

choices.text: Read the headings aloud before comparing

outcomes.text: You read the headings aloud, with help when a word defeats you. The two copies are easier to compare once you know what each column records.

choices.text: Prepare lengths of cord for the writing board

outcomes.text: You measure and tie cord for carrying the writing board. The calculator tests it before moving the lists to the next room.

choices.text: Leave the copies on the table

outcomes.text: You leave the calculator bent over the two lists and return to your own work.

events.title: A vessel for another house
events.text: A finished vessel rocks inside its packing. The workshop needs it delivered whole and has more preparation work to come. A worker offers smaller tasks alongside a place for a new apprentice.

choices.text: Take the supervised workshop apprenticeship

outcomes.text: You take the workshop's preparation place. The worker gives you the first materials to arrange and shows where the tools are kept.

choices.text: Shape soft supports around the vessel

outcomes.text: You fit soft supports around the vessel's uneven outline. The worker steadies it while you close the remaining gaps.

choices.text: Practise securing the light practice load

outcomes.text: You secure a light practice bundle before touching the customer's vessel. The worker pulls at the cord and shows where it still slips.

choices.text: Compare the packed items with the receipt

outcomes.text: You check the labels and count the packed items with the worker. The receipt agrees before anything leaves the workshop.

choices.text: Leave the packing to the worker

outcomes.text: You move away from the vessel. The worker reaches for another piece of packing.

events.title: A message before rehearsal
events.text: A performer has not yet sent word about a household engagement. Props lie in pieces beside the rehearsal space. There is paid message work, or you can stay to help the performance take shape.

choices.text: Deliver the agreed local message for 10 drachmas

outcomes.text: You deliver the agreed message, wait for the reply and bring it back without losing a word. The performer pays your household 10 drachmas.

choices.text: Help fit and arrange the wooden props

outcomes.text: You fit the wooden props while a worker checks the joins. The performers can finally rehearse with them in place.

choices.text: Stay to practise a sequence of musical cues

outcomes.text: You repeat the entrances until each performer knows when the next will begin. The sequence holds through a full rehearsal.

choices.text: Leave them to rehearse

outcomes.text: You go back to your other tasks as the performers start the opening once more.

events.title: The count before the delivery
events.text: A delivery waits beside the shop counter, with its receipt still unchecked. The owner has regular accounts work for a capable clerk. There is also a small parcel to carry and packing to inspect.

choices.text: Take regular work checking the shop's accounts

outcomes.text: You take the shop's regular clerk work and begin checking its accounts. The first delivery record is already waiting on the counter.

choices.text: Carry and count a small local delivery for 10 drachmas

outcomes.text: You count the light parcel with a worker and take it to the nearby recipient. You bring back the acknowledgment and receive 10 drachmas.

choices.text: Check the practice knots used in packing

outcomes.text: You test the spare practice knots beside the packing. The worker shows why one holds and another opens under a pull.

choices.text: Practise reading the receipt's labels

outcomes.text: A reader helps you separate the names from the quantities. By the end, you can follow the short receipt without losing your place.

choices.text: Pass on the shop's work

outcomes.text: You leave the parcel and receipt on the counter. The owner calls for another helper.

events.title: The measure at the bench
events.text: The workshop's bench is crowded with a wooden fitting, finished pots and packing still to be cut. A potter could take regular work here. The smaller tasks also need hands before the delivery leaves.

choices.text: Take the workshop's regular pottery work

outcomes.text: You begin regular pottery work for the workshop. There are vessels waiting for you beyond the crowded preparation bench.

choices.text: Prepare a carefully measured wooden fitting

outcomes.text: You mark the wood, measure again and fit it under the worker's eye. A small correction brings the edges together.

choices.text: Arrange a clear order for the packing tasks

outcomes.text: You put the light tasks in an order the helpers can follow. The final count agrees with the prepared bundles.

choices.text: Prepare soft packing for 10 drachmas

outcomes.text: You cut and arrange the soft packing. The worker checks it around the vessels before paying your 10 drachmas.

choices.text: Keep to your other work

outcomes.text: You leave the busy bench to the workshop's helpers and go back to your own tasks.

events.title: Two accounts of one job
events.text: Two adults set down their records of the same short job. The columns and the explanations disagree, and each points to the other's copy. They need someone to check before they argue any further.

choices.text: Read both accounts and compare their reasons

outcomes.text: With a reader's help, you compare the wording. You point out the claim that neither account has yet explained.

choices.text: Check the numbered columns

outcomes.text: You count down the columns until one entry has slipped beneath the wrong heading. The disagreement in the numbers becomes easier to locate.

choices.text: Prepare a clean checked copy for 10 drachmas

outcomes.text: A reader checks as you prepare a clean copy from the two accounts. The household pays 10 drachmas for the finished work.

choices.text: Leave the records with their owners

outcomes.text: You set the two copies down. The adults return to comparing them, a little more quietly.

events.title: The part another voice could take
events.text: The performers are rehearsing for household engagements and need another musician. They will hear you before offering regular work. The entrances and the introduction also need putting in order.

choices.text: Take regular work as a hired musician

outcomes.text: You join the paid rehearsals and engagements. The part that needed another musician is now yours to prepare.

choices.text: Practise the agreed entries before applying

outcomes.text: You repeat the entrances with the ensemble. The others stop at the missed cues and give you room to try them again.

choices.text: Read the short introduction for the gathering

outcomes.text: A reader checks the introduction while you practise it aloud. You agree on the words the gathering needs to hear before the music.

choices.text: Help agree a clear rehearsal order

outcomes.text: You break the rehearsal into short sections and agree who enters next. Less of the afternoon disappears in starting over.

choices.text: Let the ensemble rehearse

outcomes.text: You step out of the rehearsal space. The performers begin the disputed passage again.

events.title: Work ashore or aboard
events.text: A merchant needs a clerk; a ship's crew needs a sailor. Their work begins at the same quay and goes in different directions. There are smaller tasks if neither place is right for you yet.

choices.text: Take the sailor's place with the crew

outcomes.text: You take a sailor's place with the crew and turn to the work aboard.

choices.text: Take the merchant's clerk position

outcomes.text: You take the merchant's clerk position and begin checking the regular accounts.

choices.text: Stay ashore to practise rope handling

outcomes.text: You stay ashore and work through the rope handling with an experienced worker. Your present arrangements remain in place.

choices.text: Check the light delivery's quantities

outcomes.text: You compare the light delivery with the list. One quantity needs another count before you are satisfied.

choices.text: Keep your present arrangements

outcomes.text: You pass on the clerk's place and the berth, and return to your existing work.

events.title: More than a clean copy
events.text: A reader has work for a copyist, but the passage on the table is causing an argument. A separate day list also waits to be checked. You can ask for the regular place or help with one of the unfinished tasks.

choices.text: Take regular work at the copying bench

outcomes.text: You take a regular place at the copying bench. The reader brings over the first sheets.

choices.text: Work through the passage with a reader

outcomes.text: You read the disputed words together and ask which reason supports the conclusion. The reader returns to a sentence they had passed over.

choices.text: Compare the intervals in a separate day list

outcomes.text: You check the intervals against the copied observations. A skipped entry accounts for the difference.

choices.text: Practise reading a short introduction aloud

outcomes.text: You practise the introduction aloud while the reader follows the words. A pause makes the difficult sentence clearer.

choices.text: Leave the reader to the passage

outcomes.text: You set down the copy and go back to your other work. The reader is still considering the difficult sentence.

events.title: A pattern to fit, an order to pack
events.text: The workshop has regular places for a potter and an apprentice. For now, a repeated wooden pattern needs fitting and a delivery needs packing. Helpers keep reaching across one another for the same materials.

choices.text: Take regular work as a potter

outcomes.text: You take regular pottery work at the workshop and begin on the waiting vessels.

choices.text: Take the supervised workshop apprenticeship

outcomes.text: You take the preparation place as an apprentice. The worker starts you with the materials needed at the bench.

choices.text: Practise fitting the repeated wooden pattern

outcomes.text: You fit a spare section of the pattern. The craft worker checks the measurements and shows where a cut needs correcting.

choices.text: Agree the order for several light packing tasks

outcomes.text: You agree on an order for the packing tasks. This time the helpers can reach their materials without crossing each other's paths.

choices.text: Pass on the workshop's offers

outcomes.text: You leave the pattern and packing to the workers already there, and keep your present arrangements.

events.title: Two unequal footprints
events.text: You compare the prints of two sandals in the dust and put your own foot beside them.

events.title: A thread across the light
events.text: A loose thread casts a thin shadow. You move your hand behind it until the two shapes line up.

events.title: An entrance without a sound
events.text: The children try a game in which everyone must notice the next person's signal before moving.

events.title: A reply folded inside
events.text: A reader unfolds a short message, reads it aloud and folds the reply differently so the household can tell them apart.

events.title: A bridge made of reeds
events.text: You place light reeds over a narrow groove in the courtyard and see which arrangement holds a harmless scrap.

events.title: The empty pitcher's echo
events.text: Someone notices that a sound changes when the pitcher is empty. You take turns listening without striking the vessel.

events.title: From the other side
events.text: A drawing looks different from the opposite side of the mat. You change places with another child to compare it.

events.title: The waiting hand
events.text: An adult holds out a hand to keep a group waiting until a narrow doorway is clear. You try the same signal in a game.

events.title: A shallow box
events.text: A shallow box appears to hold more counters than a deeper one. You spread them out and see the difference.

events.title: The refrain everyone knows
events.text: Several voices join a familiar refrain from different parts of the room. You listen for where each one enters.

events.title: Room for the long cord
events.text: A worker coils a long cord before carrying it. You watch the pile take less space without becoming shorter.

events.title: The old correction
events.text: A reader points out an earlier correction on a practice scrap. You can still see why the first mark was confusing.

events.title: A figure seen from below
events.text: A maker sets a small figure on a high shelf and asks you to look from the floor. The face disappears into its chest. Your old interest in shaping things draws you closer; together, you turn the head until its expression can be seen.

events.title: The reason changes over supper
events.text: A discussion over supper turns on a rule everyone first calls fair. You ask for the reason, as you have liked doing since childhood. One guest changes the example; another puts down their cup and begins their answer again.

events.title: The bundle that keeps slipping
events.text: A crew member struggles with a bundle whose cord slides whenever it is lifted. Your early interest in ropes and loads makes you stop to watch. You help steady the practice bundle while they show how to place the next turn under tension.

events.title: One signal, understood
events.text: A retired guard watches several helpers block a narrow passage, each following a different shouted instruction. Knowing your interest in coordinated tasks, they show you a clear hand signal. You try it with the group, and the next load passes through without a quarrel.

events.title: The entry counted twice
events.text: A stallholder compares a short list with the goods and frowns at a missing measure. You have long liked checking quantities, so you look along with them. The same entry appears twice; you separate the totals and help check the count again.

events.title: Another mark beside the shadow
events.text: A reader lays two sets of shadow marks side by side. Your early interest in intervals and records pulls you into the comparison. You count the spaces aloud, spot a skipped interval and help place a fresh mark for the next observation.

events.title: They ask for the phrase again
events.text: At a household gathering, a familiar musical phrase loses its final beat in the noise. Your childhood interest in rhythm makes the gap hard to ignore. You repeat the phrase; two listeners join at the right moment and ask you to lead it once more.

events.title: A stone offcut on the spare bench
events.text: A sculptor has cleared a spare bench and set a stone offcut beside it. For 90 drachmas, you can use the shared tools and spend several sessions learning to cut a relief under supervision. It is a practice place, not a customer commission.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 90 drachmas to join the relief workshop

outcomes.text: You pay for the bench and spend the sessions testing how shallow a cut can still catch the light. The sculptor makes you redo one uneven edge. You take the practice piece home, with no customer commission attached.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to join the relief workshop

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the bench and spend the sessions testing how shallow a cut can still catch the light. The sculptor makes you redo one uneven edge. You take the practice piece home, with no customer commission attached.

events.title: A question with room for another reader
events.text: A reader is gathering a small circle to compare arguments about keeping promises. Eighty drachmas will cover the copied extracts and guided meetings. You can take the place or leave it and continue your ordinary reading.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 80 drachmas to join the study circle

outcomes.text: You pay for the extracts and read your objection aloud. Another reader finds a case you had missed, and you revise the outline before the next meeting. The sessions are preparation, rather than a teaching appointment.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to join the study circle

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the extracts and read your objection aloud. Another reader finds a case you had missed, and you revise the outline before the next meeting. The sessions are preparation, rather than a teaching appointment.

events.title: A practice berth before departure
events.text: A crew can take you on a short supervised passage for 100 drachmas, covering the berth, meals and practice materials. An experienced hand will check your work aboard. This berth pays no wage and carries no cargo-profit share.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 100 drachmas to take the practice berth

outcomes.text: You pay for the berth and work through lashings, a shared watch and the load list with an experienced hand. The corrections are immediate, sometimes repeated. You return with practice, rather than a paid delivery to your name.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to take the practice berth

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the berth and work through lashings, a shared watch and the load list with an experienced hand. The corrections are immediate, sometimes repeated. You return with practice, rather than a paid delivery to your name.

events.title: The veteran repeats the signal
events.text: A veteran sets out worn practice gear and demonstrates a signal that is easily misunderstood. Eighty drachmas buys several sessions using the space and equipment. The lessons offer preparation; they promise neither enlistment nor rank.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 80 drachmas to arrange the veteran's sessions

outcomes.text: You pay for the sessions and repeat the signal until the others respond to the same instruction. The veteran checks your equipment list and makes you explain one confusing order again. You leave better prepared, without a military appointment.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to arrange the veteran's sessions

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the sessions and repeat the signal until the others respond to the same instruction. The veteran checks your equipment list and makes you explain one confusing order again. You leave better prepared, without a military appointment.

events.title: The trader keeps the old receipts
events.text: A trader offers to teach you from a set of practice supply accounts. For 90 drachmas, you can compare the receipts and work through the disputed entries together. The fee buys instruction and copies, not stock or a promise of profit.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 90 drachmas to study the supply accounts

outcomes.text: You pay for the copies and spread the receipts in order. The trader asks you to explain a disputed total before showing where the error began. You finish the lessons with corrected accounts, but no goods or customer order of your own.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to study the supply accounts

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the copies and spread the receipts in order. The trader asks you to explain a disputed total before showing where the error began. You finish the lessons with corrected accounts, but no goods or customer order of your own.

events.title: A place at the measuring table
events.text: A table reader has room for another learner beside the measuring materials. One hundred drachmas pays for copied tables, materials and several supervised sessions. You will compare recorded intervals and calculations; the place promises no knowledge of future events.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 100 drachmas to join the table-reading sessions

outcomes.text: You pay for the sessions and check one column against the recorded intervals. The reader stops at an uncertain seasonal entry and asks you to distinguish it from a calculation. Your corrected exercise remains practice, rather than a published table.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to join the table-reading sessions

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the sessions and check one column against the recorded intervals. The reader stops at an uncertain seasonal entry and asks you to distinguish it from a calculation. Your corrected exercise remains practice, rather than a published table.

events.title: One place left at rehearsal
events.text: An ensemble has room for another performer in a short course of rehearsals. Eighty drachmas covers the shared room, borrowed equipment and instruction. The practice place is available, though it comes with no paid engagement.

choices.text: Leave the opportunity for now

outcomes.text: You leave the optional place for someone else. You pay nothing, take no loan and can continue your usual practice.

choices.text: Pay 80 drachmas to join the ensemble rehearsals

outcomes.text: You pay for the rehearsals and learn to wait for the entrance instead of rushing it. The lead performer repeats the difficult phrase until you fit it with the others. The rehearsal ends without a paid engagement, but the passage is steadier.

choices.text: Ask the moneylender for cash to join the ensemble rehearsals

outcomes.text: You accept the moneylender's stated repayment terms and use the borrowed cash for the place. You pay for the rehearsals and learn to wait for the entrance instead of rushing it. The lead performer repeats the difficult phrase until you fit it with the others. The rehearsal ends without a paid engagement, but the passage is steadier.

events.title: Experienced hands put your work to the test
events.text: People who know your earlier work invite you to attempt a demanding demonstration in your strongest practical field. They will check the details, question your decisions and ask you to repeat anything uncertain. Years of practice give you a chance; acceptance is not assured.

choices.text: Keep to your present work

outcomes.text: You decline the demonstration and continue the work you already know. No fee or new obligation is taken on.

choices.text: Bring a difficult public discussion to an exact conclusion

outcomes.text: You hear each objection, separate the disputed points and answer without losing the thread. The listeners can repeat the agreement in the same terms. Your command of public speaking reaches its cap.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already exceptionally developed
You use these methods in your regular work

outcomes.text: The listeners follow most of your case, but one unresolved objection returns. You work through that passage again and practise a clearer answer.

choices.text: Reconcile a difficult account from independent records

outcomes.text: You trace the quantities through independently kept records, explain every discrepancy and verify the final totals by another method. Reckoning reaches its cap.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already exceptionally developed
You use these methods in your regular work

outcomes.text: You reconcile the main totals, but an unexplained entry remains. Another reader helps you trace its origin and check that part of the calculation.

choices.text: Plan and lead a demanding supervised passage

outcomes.text: You explain the sail plan, organize each watch and adjust the work as the conditions change. The experienced hands agree that every check was completed in time. Seamanship reaches its cap.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already exceptionally developed
You use these methods in your regular work

outcomes.text: The passage is completed, but an experienced hand must correct the timing of one maneuver. You practise the sequence again and discuss the earlier signs you missed.

choices.text: Demonstrate a veteran's command of a difficult field exercise

outcomes.text: Drawing on your earlier service, you coordinate the exercise, keep the instructions clear and account for every group and piece of equipment. The veterans accept the demonstration without a correction. Warfare reaches its cap; no new rank is awarded.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already exceptionally developed
You use these methods in your regular work

outcomes.text: The exercise exposes a confused instruction between two groups. You review it with the veterans, then practise a signal that avoids the same mistake.

choices.text: Lead an exacting performance checked by experienced musicians

outcomes.text: You carry the demanding passages cleanly, respond to the other players and bring each entrance together. The musicians accept the performance as an example for their future work. Music reaches its cap.

weightModifiers.reason: Your technique is already exceptionally developed
You use these methods in your regular work

outcomes.text: The performance holds together, but the musicians identify a rough transition. You rehearse the difficult entrance slowly before trying the passage again.

events.title: Waiting for the last sling
events.text: The last load hangs above the quay while two workers argue over its weight. A harbour worker steps into your patch of shade and remarks that the argument has lasted longer than the unloading.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You give your name, and the worker gives theirs. By the time the sling is moving again, you have exchanged enough stories to recognise each other another day.

events.title: A conversation above the quay
events.text: {person:person-harbor} sees you above the quay and leaves room on the low wall. The talk begins with a delayed boat, then wanders into things neither of you came here to discuss.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-harbor} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-harbor}

outcomes.text: You stay until the argument on the quay has finally ended. {person:person-harbor} laughs that you have both wasted the same hour, and you agree to seek each other out again as friends.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-harbor} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-harbor} smiles and agrees to meet without an errand to excuse it. You settle on a day and begin dating.
{person:person-harbor} would rather keep the acquaintance as it is. You accept the answer and let the talk return to the boats.

events.title: Room under the awning
events.text: A brief shower drives you beneath a market awning. A seller pulls a basket aside to make room, then asks whether you found the thing you came for.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You trade names while the rain taps the awning. The seller tells you which stall to try next; you promise to report whether the advice was any good.

events.title: The errand can wait
events.text: {person:person-market} spots you passing the stalls and calls you over. You compare the morning's purchases, then carry on talking after the shopping is settled.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-market} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-market}

outcomes.text: The next errand waits while you and {person:person-market} exchange the rest of your news. You agree to keep meeting as friends, even on days when neither needs anything from the market.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-market} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-market} agrees to a date and suggests a time when neither of you will be watching a stall. You part with a plan to spend time together.
{person:person-market} shakes their head kindly; they do not want to date. You accept it, and the conversation returns to the price of the morning's goods.

events.title: While the binding dries
events.text: A worker has finished binding a repaired handle and warns you not to test it yet. There is a place to sit beside the bench while it dries.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You ask how the handle broke and soon exchange names. The binding is ready before either of you has finished the conversation; you agree to talk another day.

events.title: The bench swept clean
events.text: {person:person-workshop} has cleared the day's shavings from the bench. There is room to sit, and for once no customer is waiting at the doorway.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-workshop} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-workshop}

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-workshop} talk until someone comes to collect a repair. Before leaving, you agree to make time for the friendship beyond these chance visits.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-workshop} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-workshop} agrees to meet after the tools are put away. You make the invitation a date and settle the time together.
{person:person-workshop} prefers to keep things friendly. You accept the answer without asking again, then help clear space for the waiting customer.

events.title: Two labels, one bundle
events.text: A linen worker asks you to hold one bundle while they compare two labels. The labels have been exchanged; putting them right leaves a moment to talk.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You exchange names while the worker fastens the correct labels. They remember how readily you held the awkward bundle and invite you to stop another time.

events.title: The last bundle tied
events.text: {person:person-linen} finishes tying a linen bundle and sits beside it. A story about the day's muddled deliveries gives you both an excuse to linger.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-linen} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-linen}

outcomes.text: You finish the story together, each remembering a different detail. You and {person:person-linen} agree that this should become a friendship, rather than another conversation snatched between bundles.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-linen} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-linen} agrees to a date once the deliveries are done. You choose a time neither of you will have to hurry away.
{person:person-linen} does not want a date, though the invitation is kindly meant. You accept the answer and ask how the muddled delivery was finally settled.

events.title: The reader is still occupied
events.text: Someone ahead of you has brought the reader a long, troublesome letter. Another visitor shifts along the seat to make room while you wait your turns.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You exchange names and complaints about waiting, keeping your private messages folded. When the reader calls, you are reluctant to interrupt the conversation.

events.title: No letter to be read today
events.text: {person:person-copies} sees you near the copying workshop. Neither of you has brought a message this time, but you stop where you once waited together.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-copies} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-copies}

outcomes.text: There is no reader to call either of you away. You and {person:person-copies} finish the conversation and agree to keep making time for one another as friends.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-copies} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-copies} agrees to a date. This time you choose to meet, rather than leave it to the reader's queue.
{person:person-copies} would rather remain an acquaintance. You accept the answer and carry on talking until it is time to go.

events.title: The loaves need another moment
events.text: The first loaves are not ready. A bakery worker leans out to explain the delay, then stays in the doorway to ask what is happening further down the street.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You exchange names and neighbourhood news until the worker is called back inside. By the time the bread appears, you have a reason to return beyond the loaf.

events.title: After the morning loaves
events.text: {person:person-bakery} has a quiet interval after the morning's baking. You begin with the day's news and find yourselves talking about what you each do when the work is finished.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-bakery} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-bakery}

outcomes.text: The next batch can wait for the moment. You and {person:person-bakery} agree to see each other as friends, with more time than these conversations in the doorway.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-bakery} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-bakery} agrees to a date after the baking is done. You settle a time that belongs to you both, rather than to the oven.
{person:person-bakery} does not want to begin dating. You accept it and finish the neighbourhood story you were halfway through.

events.title: A jar steadied in the queue
events.text: Your jar tilts as the queue moves. Someone catches its shoulder, sets it straight and remarks that the waiting is easier with two people to complain about it.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You exchange names before your turns arrive. When the jars are filled, you walk part of the way together and agree to look out for one another again.

events.title: Two jars set down
events.text: You meet {person:person-well} near the water queue and set your jars safely aside. The queue moves on while your conversation finds a different subject.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-well} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-well}

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-well} make room for a longer conversation after the water is carried home. You agree to keep meeting as friends, whether or not your errands coincide.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-well} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-well} agrees to a date when neither of you is carrying a full jar. You choose a time and leave pleased with the arrangement.
{person:person-well} would rather keep your meetings friendly. You accept the answer and help clear the way for the next person with a jar.

events.title: The stools after the music
events.text: The gathering has ended, but the stools still crowd the courtyard. Another guest takes one end of a stack while you take the other; the last row gives you time to compare the music.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You exchange names over the final stack of stools. The other guest recalls a different part of the performance, and you agree to finish the argument another day.

events.title: A tune neither of you has forgotten
events.text: {person:person-festival} recognises you before you reach the courtyard. You both remember the same gathering, though you disagree about which song was best.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-festival} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-festival}

outcomes.text: Neither of you wins the argument about the music. You and {person:person-festival} agree to keep meeting as friends, giving yourselves plenty of time to disagree again.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-festival} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-festival} agrees to a date and offers to meet before the next gathering gets crowded. You begin making plans for time together.
{person:person-festival} enjoys the conversation but does not want to date. You accept the distinction and return to your unfinished argument about the song.

events.title: The question after the reading
events.text: The reader has finished, but one listener is still puzzling over a passage. You hear the question as you leave and stop to offer what you thought it meant.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: Your answers differ enough to keep you both talking. You exchange names before parting, so the next discussion will not begin with strangers.

events.title: A passage carried into the street
events.text: {person:person-library} finds you after a reading and returns to a question from your last conversation. Soon you are comparing your own experiences instead of the reader's words.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-library} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-library}

outcomes.text: The discussion runs beyond the passage that began it. You and {person:person-library} agree to meet as friends, with no reading needed to bring you together.

choices.text: Ask {person:person-library} on a date

outcomes.text: {person:person-library} agrees to a date. You choose to spend an afternoon together and leave the next reading out of the plan.
{person:person-library} would rather keep the conversations as they are. You accept the answer and finish discussing the passage before you part.

events.title: Everyone came in too early
events.text: A rehearsal breaks up amid laughter about one disastrous entrance. A performer beside you insists that the cue was late; from where you stood, it looked rather different.

choices.text: Finish your errand and go

outcomes.text: You finish what brought you here and go on your way.

choices.text: Stay and introduce yourself

outcomes.text: You exchange names while defending your versions of the missed cue. Neither quite concedes, but you agree to look for each other after another rehearsal.

events.title: After the instruments are put away
events.text: {person:person-music} stays behind after rehearsal and asks what you heard from your side of the room. Your different accounts of the music become an excuse to keep talking.

choices.text: Enjoy a short chat and go

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-music} exchange news and part without making new plans.

choices.text: Become friends with {person:person-music}

outcomes.text: You and {person:person-music} agree that the missed entrance has earned enough argument for one day. You make plans to meet as friends when there is no rehearsal to review.

events.title: An order during the succession struggles
events.text: Your unit is ordered to guard a supply route while rival commanders dispute authority after Alexander's death. The assignment is local and uncertain: one post covers the stores; another stands farther along an exposed approach.

choices.text: Guard the stores and move supplies

outcomes.text: You guard the stores and help move loads into a protected yard.

choices.text: Volunteer for the exposed post (risk of death)

outcomes.text: You return from the post with a damaged shield and a clearer understanding of the unit's movements.
A spear strikes your abdomen during the assignment. Blood loss from the wound proves fatal.

events.title: The loads and the equipment
events.text: The unit checks a storehouse and compares its equipment list with the incoming loads. The names at the head of the orders may change; every missing item still has to be explained.

events.title: A passage to Athens
events.text: A returning trader offers to arrange a passage to Athens and a place to stay with readers there. Aristotle is teaching at the Lyceum. Taking the journey would mean a season away from your household; a place in a discussion is not promised.

choices.text: Stay with your household and local teacher

outcomes.text: You ask for a copied argument instead and keep your work near home. This time you do not travel to Athens.

choices.text: Pay 30 drachmas for the round trip to Athens

outcomes.text: In Athens, a reader brings you into a discussion at the Lyceum. Aristotle asks the group to distinguish what a thing is from why it changes. You return to Egypt with a checked set of notes and a question your own teacher cannot dismiss.

The passage reaches Athens late, and the promised introduction does not materialize. Other readers help you examine an argument before you return to Egypt. You have made the journey, but have not heard Aristotle himself.

events.title: Supplies for the king's party
events.text: Alexander's party is inspecting the Egyptian coast. An officer needs local hands to check boat loads and clear a landing. Helping could put you near the king, but a paid task is not an introduction to him.

choices.text: Keep to your existing work

outcomes.text: You leave the officer to find other hands. The party's plans reach you through the people who took the work.

choices.text: Check the loads and help prepare the landing

outcomes.text: You count the loads, clear the landing and receive the agreed payment. The officer keeps your name with the supply account; the work becomes part of the preparations around the new city.

choices.text: Take the work and ask to present the checked account

outcomes.text: After the loads are checked, an officer calls you forward with the account. Alexander asks whether boats can use the landing in a contrary wind. You answer from the shore you know. The exchange is brief; afterward you return to the workers and collect your pay.
The officer accepts the account and pays you, but the king's party moves on before you are called. Your work is recorded; you have not spoken to Alexander.

events.title: The line that the sketch cannot prove
events.text: A reader connected with Euclid's teaching brings you a geometrical construction. A neat drawing will not answer the question: you must explain why the steps hold. Ten drachmas would cover materials and time in the working circle.

choices.text: Keep to the calculations you already use

outcomes.text: You return the construction and finish the accounts waiting on your own table.

choices.text: Pay 10 drachmas and work through the demonstration

outcomes.text: In the teaching circle, Euclid stops at the step you thought was obvious. You rebuild it from the agreed definitions and earlier results. When the demonstration is accepted, you take home a corrected copy whose margin records the point you had to prove.

The readers find a step your explanation does not justify. You leave with a correction to work through, rather than an accepted demonstration. The fee and the failed attempt have still bought a clearer question.

sources.title: Strabo, Geography 17.1.3–10: the Nile and Alexandria
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; H. L. Jones, Loeb translation (1932)
sources.period: Augustan-era account of Egypt and Alexandria, referring also to earlier Ptolemaic history
sources.geography: Alexandria and the Nile valley
sources.summary: Describes Alexandria's harbors, Pharos, streets and royal district, and the importance of Nile inundation, canals and agricultural management.
sources.limitations: Elite literary testimony with Roman imperial sympathies. Descriptive claims and reported numbers are not a population survey, an exact city map or annual household probabilities.

sources.title: Bellum Alexandrinum 1–33: the Alexandrian War
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; Loeb translation (1955)
sources.period: Events of 48–47 BCE; authorship traditionally associated with the Caesarian corpus
sources.geography: Alexandria and the Nile Delta
sources.summary: Narrates fighting, barricades, harbor operations and disruption of Caesar's water supply during the Alexandrian War.
sources.limitations: A partisan Roman military narrative with prejudicial descriptions of Alexandrians. It supports a war setting, not invented civilian experiences, precise casualty odds or a claim that the entire Library was destroyed.

sources.title: Chronological Tables for Caesar's Wars (58–45 BCE)
sources.publisher: John T. Ramsey and Kurt A. Raaflaub, Histos 11 (2017); journal page published online 2018
sources.period: 58–45 BCE, including the Alexandrian War of 48–47 BCE
sources.geography: Roman campaigns including Alexandria and Egypt
sources.summary: Reconstructs the sequence of Caesar's campaigns and separates Roman civil-calendar dates from reconstructed Julian dates.
sources.limitations: A scholarly chronology reconstructed from ancient testimony. Day-level dates may be disputed; the game uses year-level anchors and does not reproduce whole tables.

sources.title: Ptolemaic Period
sources.publisher: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.period: 332–30 BCE; Actium in 31 BCE and the end of Ptolemaic rule in 30 BCE
sources.geography: Egypt, with Alexandria as capital
sources.summary: Provides a heritage-authority overview of Ptolemaic Egypt and the transition following the defeat at Actium.
sources.limitations: A broad public-history overview, not a detailed social dataset. Use the year-level chronology without treating its compressed narrative as proof of every personal consequence.

sources.title: Augustus, Res Gestae, especially section 27
sources.publisher: Livius.org; F. W. Shipley translation from LacusCurtius
sources.period: Augustus's retrospective inscription, completed near the end of his reign in 14 CE
sources.geography: Roman Empire; section 27 concerns annexation of Egypt
sources.summary: Augustus claims to have added Egypt to Roman rule. The inscription offers a contemporary imperial voice for the political transition.
sources.limitations: Self-promotional imperial testimony. It does not describe the response of all Egyptians and must be paired with independent chronology and local evidence.

sources.title: Alexandrian Documents from the Reign of Augustus
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, Department of Classics, University of Cincinnati
sources.period: Augustan Alexandria, especially 13 BCE; individual texts and later additions have their own dates
sources.geography: Documents issued in Alexandria, many recovered from reused cartonnage at Abusir el-Melek
sources.summary: Provides scholarly English translations of Alexandrian contracts, letters, petitions and association records, with document identifiers and links to the underlying Greek texts.
sources.limitations: The surviving archive is selective, not representative of every household. Early Roman material is comparative evidence for earlier Ptolemaic years; use each document's actual date.

sources.title: BGU 4.1125.1–15: apprenticeship contract for a musician
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: March/April 13 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Records training in flute playing, the term of apprenticeship, provision of food and clothing, and examination by fellow practitioners.
sources.limitations: The apprentice is enslaved, and this is a specific musical contract. It is evidence for organized training, not universal schooling or the terms of a free child's scribal apprenticeship.

sources.title: BGU 4.1058: wetnursing contract
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: 30 March 13 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Documents paid nursing, infant care and a clause anticipating the possibility of a child's death.
sources.limitations: Both nurse and infant are enslaved in this contract. Its clauses show contemporary concerns; they do not estimate infant mortality or demonstrate that every household employed a wet nurse.

sources.title: BGU 4.1052.1–34: marriage contract
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: 15 April 13 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Records an agreement for a shared life, a dowry and economic and marital obligations.
sources.limitations: One Greek-language legal agreement, with particular status and guardianship conventions. Its terms are not universal Egyptian marriage rules or an observed marriage-age distribution.

sources.title: BGU 4.1141: private letter
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: After 9 April 13 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Preserves correspondence concerning friendship, accusations, work, wages and interpersonal obligations.
sources.limitations: A fragmentary and sometimes difficult personal letter, embedded in unequal relationships. It supports written communication as a theme, not the fictional character's letter or a literacy rate.

sources.title: BGU 4.1117: lease contract for a bakery
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: April/May 13 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria, Beta quarter
sources.summary: Describes a bakery lease, equipment, rent, repairs and responsibility for taxes, illustrating workshop livelihoods and contractual obligations.
sources.limitations: A single bakery agreement. Monetary amounts and conditions cannot be generalized to all trades or converted directly into the game's abstract wealth score.

sources.title: BGU 4.1151.1–18: partial payment of an inheritance
sources.publisher: Peter van Minnen, University of Cincinnati, translation of the primary papyrus
sources.period: 12 April 13 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Records an agreement concerning the partial payment of an inheritance, supporting a narrative theme of property and obligations between generations.
sources.limitations: A particular legal settlement. It supplies neither a representative inheritance amount nor evidence that all older people held transferable property.

sources.title: Education and Apprenticeship
sources.publisher: Nikolaos Lazaridis (2010), UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology
sources.period: Survey across ancient Egyptian periods, including Ptolemaic and Roman bilingual education
sources.geography: Ancient Egypt; not exclusively Alexandria
sources.summary: Reviews training for scribes and specialist crafts, educational exercises and restricted access to formal schooling.
sources.limitations: A long-period synthesis with uneven evidence. It cannot supply exact Alexandrian enrolment or literacy probabilities, and does not justify giving every child formal schooling.

sources.title: Funerary Rituals (Ptolemaic and Roman Periods)
sources.publisher: Christina Riggs (2010), UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology; University of East Anglia repository
sources.period: Ptolemaic and Roman periods
sources.geography: Egypt; evidence includes Akhmim, Thebes, Tuna el-Gebel and other communities
sources.summary: Surveys burial, commemoration, mourning and funerary associations, including arrangements for members to contribute to funeral costs.
sources.limitations: Rites varied with community, status, resources and religion. Elite mummification evidence is not a universal Alexandrian funeral script; use broad remembrance themes carefully.

sources.title: The abuse of aged parents in the ancient Roman world
sources.publisher: Tim Parkin, Bulletin of the Institute of Classical Studies 66(2), 41–50; online 2024
sources.period: Roman world with Ptolemaic Egyptian petitions of 225 and 221 BCE among the comparative cases
sources.geography: Roman Mediterranean and the Arsinoite nome in Egypt
sources.summary: Examines duties, dependence and care between generations, including papyrus petitions by older parents.
sources.limitations: Sparse, often one-sided dispute evidence from varied times and places. It does not establish rates of neglect or a uniform old-age household arrangement in Alexandria.

sources.title: Volcanic suppression of Nile summer flooding triggers revolt and constrains interstate conflict in ancient Egypt
sources.publisher: Joseph G. Manning and colleagues (2017), Nature Communications 8, 900; author copy at UC Berkeley
sources.period: Ptolemaic Egypt, 305–30 BCE, with later Nilometer measurements used for comparison
sources.geography: Nile basin and Egypt; papyrus survival particularly strong in the Fayyum
sources.summary: Combines environmental reconstructions and ancient writings to examine Nile flood variability, agricultural vulnerability and social stress.
sources.limitations: Ancient flood indications are intermittent and may have dating uncertainty. The continuous Nilometer series begins in 622 CE; this is not a precise annual Alexandrian food-price or famine-risk dataset.

sources.title: Roman Model Life Table (Coale–Demeny Female West Level 3)
sources.publisher: Columbia University / W. V. Harris teaching resources
sources.period: Comparative Roman demographic model; not an observed Ptolemaic cohort
sources.geography: Roman comparison model; not an Alexandria-specific dataset
sources.summary: Provides age-band mortality, survivorship and remaining life expectancy for a model population with life expectancy at birth of 25 years.
sources.limitations: A female model life table, not measured male Alexandrian rates. Converting interval death probabilities into annual hazards assumes within-band timing. Age at death is simulated, not a historical prediction.

sources.title: Quantifying antiquity
sources.publisher: Roger S. Bagnall, Columbia University
sources.period: Contrasts Roman Egyptian census evidence with Hellenistic Egyptian household lists
sources.geography: Egypt, with wider methodological comparisons
sources.summary: Explains the promise and limits of ancient demographic evidence, including why Hellenistic household lists without ages cannot yield life expectancy.
sources.limitations: A methodological essay rather than a downloadable life table. It explicitly cautions against combining Roman and Hellenistic evidence without careful analysis.

sources.title: Life Expectancy
sources.publisher: Sonia Zakrzewski (2015), UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology
sources.period: Long-period review of ancient Egyptian demographic evidence, including Roman model tables
sources.geography: Egypt; evidence from varied populations and sites
sources.summary: Explains demographic methods and biases. Table 1 reproduces a model life table for Roman Egyptian females after Bagnall and Frier (1994), with life expectancy at birth of 22.5 years.
sources.limitations: A later-period female model inferred using census returns and Coale–Demeny West, not observed mortality for a male in Ptolemaic Alexandria. Annual interpolation and the final age-band policy are additional game assumptions; cause-of-death rates are not supplied.

sources.title: Zodiaque de Dendéra (E 13482)
sources.publisher: Musée du Louvre, Egyptian Antiquities collection
sources.period: 50 BCE; catalogue dates the relief to June–August
sources.geography: Hathor temple, Dendera, Upper Egypt
sources.summary: Catalogues a sandstone ceiling relief with zodiacal signs, decans and constellations, providing a contemporary example of Egyptian astral imagery.
sources.limitations: A temple object from Dendera, not an Alexandrian teaching manual. It supplies neither access probabilities nor evidence that astrological predictions were reliable.

sources.title: Alexandrian terracottas
sources.publisher: Vatican Museums, Gregorian Egyptian Museum
sources.period: Ptolemaic and Roman periods
sources.geography: Alexandria; collection objects have varied acquisition histories
sources.summary: Describes Alexandrian figurative terracottas, including mould-made examples and a range of decorative and religious subjects.
sources.limitations: The collection spans multiple periods and some objects entered through the antiquities market. It does not measure workshop employment, wages or apprenticeship access.

sources.title: Statuette of an ancestral king (2003.154)
sources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.period: Late Period–Early Ptolemaic Period, 380–246 BCE
sources.geography: Egypt; exact workshop not established in this catalogue entry
sources.summary: Documents a carved wooden ritual figure associated with temple equipment, illustrating skilled Egyptian wood carving.
sources.limitations: Earlier than the player's lifetime and not specifically Alexandrian. The object's interpretation is debated; it does not establish a universal carving curriculum or job ladder.

sources.title: An enigmatic early horoscope: BKT X 29 (P. 11831)
sources.publisher: Berlin Papyrus Database, Egyptian Museum and Papyrus Collection; Marius Gerhardt, Andreas Winkler and Michael Zellmann-Rohrer
sources.period: Late Ptolemaic or early Roman handwriting; astronomical reconstruction best fits 5 June 29 BCE
sources.geography: Egypt; no Alexandrian workshop identified
sources.summary: Examines a Greek horoscope listing astral positions, abbreviations, the ascendant and midheaven, with possible professional or client use.
sources.limitations: The papyrus lacks a personal name and explicit date, and its solar position conflicts with the proposed reconstruction. Its use is uncertain, and no accompanying interpretation survives.

sources.title: Plutarch, Life of Antony 80: Areius and Octavian at Alexandria
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; Bernadotte Perrin, Loeb translation
sources.period: Later biography describing the Roman takeover of Alexandria in 30 BCE
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Depicts the philosopher Areius receiving public favour from Octavian and interceding for others, illustrating elite intellectual patronage and political access.
sources.limitations: A retrospective literary account, not an administrative record or promotion dataset. It concerns an exceptional elite figure and does not prove ordinary access to Cleopatra's court.

sources.title: Coins in Egypt: Coins of the Ptolemies
sources.publisher: University College London, Digital Egypt for Universities
sources.period: Ptolemaic Egypt, with an overview of earlier coinage
sources.geography: Egypt
sources.summary: Introduces Ptolemaic coin circulation, drachma denominations, bronze and silver coinage, and debt settlement as part of the economy.
sources.limitations: An overview of money and denominations, not an Alexandrian household budget or price series. It does not support the game's prices, wages, asset valuations, fixed returns or a constant currency standard across Roman rule; these remain disclosed gameplay assumptions.

sources.title: LGPN-Egypt: personal names in Egypt
sources.publisher: University of Oxford, Lexicon of Greek Personal Names
sources.period: Current completed coverage: Lower Egypt and the Fayum from the seventh century BCE to 30 BCE; the wider project extends into Roman Egypt
sources.geography: Egypt, with current database coverage focused on Lower Egypt and the Fayum
sources.summary: Introduces a source-based naming database that records personal names alongside attested occupations, dates, family connections and provenance. It supports a varied Greek-language and Egyptian-rendered naming context for fictional characters.
sources.limitations: The game does not reproduce database individuals or claim that every selected name is attested in Alexandria in 66 BCE. Names are not demographic weights, ethnic labels, gender rules or evidence that an occupation belonged to a particular community. Household profiles and event rewards remain authored fiction.

sources.title: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History 1.81.7: childhood learning and livelihood
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius, University of Chicago; C. H. Oldfather, Loeb translation (1933)
sources.period: First-century BCE literary account of Egyptian customs
sources.geography: Egypt generally; not an Alexandrian household survey
sources.summary: Describes children learning livelihood skills from fathers and relatives, alongside limited and uneven access to literacy instruction.
sources.limitations: A generalizing literary account without numerical starting ages. It supports learning and work overlapping in childhood, not the game's exact age gates, wage amounts, universal schooling or an identical experience across households.

sources.title: BGU 4.1124: cancellation of a nailsmith's apprenticeship
sources.publisher: University of Cincinnati, Ancient Alexandria documentary translations
sources.period: After June/July 18 BCE, under early Roman rule
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Records Hermaiskos, a son not yet of age, being trained in nailsmithing; cancelling the agreement permits his father to place him with another master.
sources.limitations: The apprentice's numerical age is unstated. The document postdates the cohort's Ptolemaic childhood and does not establish age 12 as a norm, free access to an apprenticeship or the game's pay and skill gains.

sources.title: BGU 4.1151.2: Loan agreement
sources.publisher: University of Cincinnati; Peter van Minnen translation
sources.period: 12 April 13 BCE, early Roman period
sources.geography: Alexandria
sources.summary: Records a money loan with scheduled instalments, default penalties and enforcement claims against debtors and workshop property.
sources.limitations: One early Roman contract, later than the Ptolemaic beginning of the game. Contractual enforcement clauses do not establish how frequently they were exercised or support violent collectors, murder, or the game's loan terms and risks.

sources.geography: Egypt and the wider Mediterranean; see the specific regional limits below

sources.publisher: Filip Coppens (2009); UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology 1(1)
sources.period: Ptolemaic and Roman periods; chiefly Upper Egyptian temple evidence
sources.geography: Egypt and the wider Mediterranean; see the specific regional limits below
sources.summary: Festival preparation, public processions, travel and distinctions between public and restricted participation. Read scope: Substantive full article, printed pp.1–8.

sources.title: World travellers: the associations of Artists of Dionysus
sources.publisher: Sophia Aneziri (2009); Wandering Poets in Ancient Greek Culture: Travel, Locality and Pan-Hellenism, Cambridge University Press; pp. 217–236; DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511576133.009
sources.period: Hellenistic professional performance networks in the wider Greek world
sources.geography: Egypt and the wider Mediterranean; see the specific regional limits below
sources.summary: Professional performance, festival networks and travel as relevant themes. Read scope: Publisher summary and metadata only.
